nodes.name: Ni foam pretreatment
nodes.procedure: The Ni foam (NF, 99.8%) that used as the support was cleaned ultrasonically in 3.0M HCl aqueous solution and ethanol (99.99%) for each 15 min sequentially, and then dried in vacuum oven at 60°C for 20 h.
nodes.source_text: The Ni foam (NF, 99.8%) that used as the support was cleaned ultrasonically in 3.0M HCl aqueous solution and ethanol (99.99%) for each 15 min sequentially, and then dried in vacuum oven at 60°C for 20 h.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of HWO
nodes.procedure: 0.2217g of (NH4)6H2W12O40·xH2O was dissolved in 30 mL of deionized water and stirred for 30 min at room temperature. Then, three pieces of the pre-treated Ni foam (20×10×1 mm) were put into the solution and stirred for another 30 min. After that, this solution and the Ni foam were transferred to a Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave. The hydrothermal process was conducted at 180°C for 24 h. After cooling down naturally, the as-prepared samples were removed and washed with deionized water for several times. Finally, a drying process was performed at 60°C for 12 h. These hydrothermally synthesized samples were denoted as HWO. The mass loading of the deposits is 27.6 mg cm^-2, which is obtained by measuring the weight difference of the foam before and after the preparation process.

nodes.name: N2 plasma treatment (0.05A)
nodes.procedure: After assembling the HWO samples on the holder, the chamber of the reactor was vacuumed to a background pressure of 2.5×10^-5 Pa. Then, N2 was passed through the chamber with a flow rate of 90 sccm. For nitrogen plasma treatment, the input current was adjusted to control the process, which determined the plasma beam intensity directly. The frequency and the duty ratio of the pulsed DC were fixed to be 60 kHz and 20%, respectively. The duration of the treatment was 20 min for each sample. The temperature was measured by a thermocouple that was attached to the specimen holder during the treatment process. With input current of 0.05±0.02A, surface temperature reached 80±10°C in steady state. The as-prepared sample is denoted as HWON-0.05.

nodes.characterization_summary: HWO, HWON-0.05, HWON-0.1, HWON-0.15 show hexagonal WO3·0.33H2O phase (PDF 00-035-1001) with peaks shifting to lower angles and broadening for HWON-0.1/0.15; HWON-0.2 shows monoclinic WO2.72 phase (PDF 01-073-2177).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The characteristic peaks of HWO, HWON-0.05, HWON-0.1 and HWON-0.15 match well with the PDF card (No. 00-035-1001)... For the case of HWON-0.2, phase transition likely occurs after the treatment...

nodes.characterization_summary: HWO shows hierarchical nanoplates (600 nm thick) with nanorod substructure (20 nm); plasma treatment rounds edges and modifies substructure - stalactite-like (HWON-0.05), sharpened (HWON-0.1), rough irregular (HWON-0.15), enlarged 150 nm (HWON-0.2).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The nanoplates were grown on the NF substrate with a thickness of about 600 nm, and the nanorod-like substructure vertically anchored on the nanoplates with a dimension of around 20 nm...
Fig. 4a shows the STEM-HAADF image of HWON-0.15, it displays a roughened morphology.

nodes.characterization_summary: HWON-0.15 shows lattice spacings of 3.86, 3.78, 2.54 Å for monoclinic WO3 (001),(020),(-122) planes and 3.92, 1.96 Å for hexagonal (001),(002) planes, slightly enlarged vs. reference.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The lattice spacing of 3.86, 3.78 and 2.54Å observed in Fig. 4b and 4c correspond to the (001), (020) and (-122) planes of monoclinic WO3...

nodes.characterization_summary: HWON-0.15 shows uniform W (21.62 at%), O (76.53 at%), N (1.84 at%) distribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy dispersive X-Ray (EDX) elemental mappings of HWON-0.15... The obtained atomic ratios of W (21.62 at%), O (76.53 at%) and N (1.84 at%) are listed in Fig. S3.

nodes.characterization_summary: O-W-O stretching bands (665, 768 cm⁻¹) blueshift with plasma intensity; phase transition to monoclinic at edges (706, 803 cm⁻¹); W=O band (952 cm⁻¹) attenuates indicating dehydration; oxygen vacancies and N-doping cause redshift and broadening.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The bands at 665 and 768 cm⁻¹ corresponding to the O-W-O stretching modes display a gradual blueshift... The frequency shift of the characteristic peak... from ∼768 cm⁻¹ to ∼802 cm⁻¹ was recognized as the phase transition...

nodes.characterization_summary: W 4f shows W⁶⁺ (35.6,37.7 eV), W⁵⁺ (34.5,36.6 eV), W⁴⁺ (33.2,35.8 eV) with increasing W⁵⁺/W⁶⁺ ratio and oxygen vacancies up to HWON-0.15; HWON-0.2 shows W-N (32.8,34.9 eV); N 1s shows N-H (402.3 eV) and W-N (397.1 eV in HWON-0.2).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution XPS W 4f spectra of the samples are shown in Fig. 6a. The peaks at 35.6 eV and 37.7 eV are assigned to W⁶⁺... For HWON-0.2, the peaks located at 32.8 eV and 34.9 eV are identified as W-N.
